clue.text: Dog racing no good for dog

parts.note: Formula One motor racing is F1, written here with I standing in for the figure 1

indicators.note: the clue asks for the word dog with G, the abbreviation for good, dropped from it

parts.note: the word taken as written before its G goes

explanation.surface: Someone thinks greyhound racing is bad for dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racing' is F1 (Formula One) with the figure read as the letter I. 'no good for' removes G (good) from DOG, leaving DO.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional stock name given to pet hounds, as Rover and Rex are.

clue.text: Dull male worried for Holmes: Watson?

parts.note: dull means flat, lifeless
ate, as in 'what's eating you?', means worried or troubled

explanation.surface: A dull man frets over what Watson means to Holmes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' is ATE in the sense of something eating at you.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr Watson shared lodgings at 221B Baker Street with Sherlock Holmes, so he was his roommate.

clue.text: Idiot cleans bug (rather than sheep)

parts.note: to dip is to plunge into a cleansing bath, as with sheep dip
a tick is a bloodsucking bug; the bracket says it is the bug, not the usual sheep, that is being dipped

explanation.surface: A fool washes an insect instead of the flock it lives on.
explanation.walkthrough: Farmers dip sheep to kill ticks; here the clue playfully dips the tick itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Dipstick is informal slang for a stupid person, a fool.

clue.text: Film Jason from Melbourne running after angry pet wallaby

indicators.note: the remaining letters come after the tantrum word

parts.note: a pet is a fit of temper, and a paddy is a British word for a tantrum

indicators.note: the film hero's surname is taken away from the city's name

parts.note: the Australian city's name taken as written
Jason Bourne is the spy hero of the Bourne films
on means running, as a machine is

explanation.surface: An Australian actor called Jason races after a cross pet wallaby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film Jason' is Bourne, not the Melbourne actor Jason Donovan the surface suggests; removing BOURNE from MELBOURNE leaves MEL. 'after' puts MEL and ON after PADDY.
explanation.definitionFit: A small scrub wallaby of Australia and New Guinea, also spelt pademelon.

clue.text: Do not apply where there's competition

parts.note: in 'they do' as an answer to 'are they?', do stands for are
N/A is short for 'not applicable'

explanation.surface: An instruction on a form: skip this where there is rivalry.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Do not apply' as 'are N/A': these things are not applicable.
explanation.definitionFit: A stadium or ring is a place where contests and sporting events are held.

clue.text: Cut up statement of Germany's EU status

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany, and 's stands for is
Germany is a member of the European Union

explanation.surface: A statement about where Germany stands in the European Union.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'statement' is 'D is member': Germany (D) is a member.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismember is to hack a body limb from limb, chopping it into pieces.

clue.text: Beginning to make nine messy single beds, one's opinion of kids?

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is wanted

parts.note: IX is nine in Roman numerals

indicators.note: messy beds are rumpled, so the letters of single beds are jumbled

explanation.surface: A parent faces making nine rumpled beds and sums up their feelings about children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messy' rearranges SINGLE BEDS into EDBLESSING, after M (first of 'make') and IX.
explanation.definitionFit: Children bring both joy and trouble, so a parent might call them a boon with drawbacks.

clue.text: Stayed off-green in sickbed

definitions.meaning: in golf, to lay up is to play deliberately short of the green

explanation.surface: A golfer kept away from the course because they were ill in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a golf shot played short of the green and being bedridden are described by this phrase.

clue.text: Source of chicken, served up in little brown thing?

definitions.text: Source of chicken, served up in little brown thing?

indicators.note: the reversed egg goes inside the little brown thing

parts.note: a nut is a small brown seed

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a chicken comes from an egg

explanation.surface: Chicken, presented in a little brown breadcrumbed piece: a fast-food snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' reverses EGG to GGE, which goes inside NUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A chicken nugget is a small breaded, browned piece of chicken meat, the whole clue's picture.

clue.text: "'eat 'em up," snarled man with frostbitten toes, once?

indicators.note: snarled means tangled, so the letters of the quoted words are knotted into a new order

explanation.surface: A man whose toes have frozen growls at someone to eat up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snarled' looks like the speech verb but rearranges EATEMUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Frostbitten toes are often removed surgically, so such a man may later have lost a limb or digit.

clue.text: Lathe knocking out first new computer

indicators.note: the earlier of the two places the letter for new appears is struck out

parts.note: a lathe is a turning machine, used to shape wood or metal

explanation.surface: A workshop lathe being dismantled to make a fresh computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking out first new' removes the first N from TURNING MACHINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Turing's theoretical device is the abstract model of every computer.

clue.text: Electronic kiss in smart phone's billets-doux?

indicators.note: the two short pieces go into the word for smart

parts.note: to smart is to sting
X is a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: An emailed kiss in the love letters sent from a smartphone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smart phone' looks like one item; 'smart' is STING.
explanation.definitionFit: Racy love messages sent by mobile phone: billets-doux are love letters.

clue.text: Maybe Kennedy's entourage fabricated monster hiding with books

indicators.note: the word for fabricated conceals the other pieces within it

parts.note: fabricated means made
OT is the Old Testament, books of the Bible
an orc is a monster from Tolkien

explanation.surface: A made-up monster concealed among books.
explanation.walkthrough: MADE hides OT and ORC: M + OTORC + ADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A presidential procession of cars, as in Dallas in 1963, is an example.

clue.text: Two score, forty apiece

definitions.meaning: the two in a pack of cards or on a die
in tennis, forty-all is called by this name

explanation.surface: Two players level on forty each.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the name for the two in cards and dice, and for forty-all in tennis.

clue.text: "The IT Crowd's baloney — endless baloney" the BBC put out

indicators.note: put out means broadcast here, but also displaced, so the letters are rearranged
the final letter of baloney is cut off

parts.note: the word taken as written before losing its end

explanation.surface: A viewer's complaint about the computing nonsense in a BBC-style sitcom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops Y from BALONEY; 'put out' rearranges BALONE with THEBBC. The IT Crowd is a British sitcom about an office computer department.
explanation.definitionFit: Jargon from computer support staff is impenetrable technical gibberish.

clue.text: Land claimed from the sea in Belgium per capita

parts.note: B is the international vehicle code for Belgium
Latin for 'by heads', so each head

explanation.surface: A statistic for Belgian land reclamation measured per person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land claimed from the sea' suggests reclamation, as in the Low Countries; it is a military landing.
explanation.definitionFit: An invading force secures a fortified position on an enemy shore after landing from ships.

clue.text: Billie Jean editor's turned over half the files for Black or White

definitions.text: half the files for Black or White

parts.note: Billie Jean King, the American tennis champion

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters are flipped to read upwards

parts.note: ED is an editor and 's stands for is

explanation.surface: An editor flips through half a dossier on Billie Jean King.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned over' reverses ED IS to SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the four files from e to h, where each king starts, form one wing of the board.

clue.text: Jelly needs a double oven, right?

indicators.note: double means the run of letters appears twice

parts.note: an Aga is a British range cooker

explanation.surface: A cook asks whether making jelly needs two ovens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double' repeats AGAR. An AGA is a heavy cast-iron range cooker common in British country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: A gelatinous substance from seaweed, used to set food and grow bacteria.

clue.text: Ticklish manager's ribs tickled

indicators.note: tickled ribs squirm about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A boss who is sensitive to being tickled has their ribs poked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ticklish' looks literal but means awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticklish can mean delicate or awkward, like a situation causing discomfort.

clue.text: Bottom I see climbing in bubble bath

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: butt is slang for bottom
oh is said when you understand

explanation.surface: Someone spots a bottom rising in a foamy bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reverses BUTTOH.
explanation.definitionFit: A heated tub of bubbling water, a jacuzzi.

clue.text: Constitutional way to oppress electors

indicators.note: in a down clue, oppressing means sitting on top of the other piece

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
the electoral roll lists voters

explanation.surface: A constitutional method for oppressing voters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constitutional' poses as the adjective about law; it is the noun for a walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A constitutional is a gentle walk taken for health.

clue.text: Teacher's falling on the rocks from here?

definitions.text: Teacher's falling on the rocks from here?

parts.words: Teacher's falling on the rocks from here?
parts.note: Teacher's is a Scotch whisky; in a pub it pours over ice from a measure fixed to the bottle

explanation.surface: A teacher plunges onto rocks from a cliff.
explanation.walkthrough: Teacher's is a brand of Scotch whisky; 'on the rocks' means over ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar measure fitted to an upturned spirit bottle dispenses a fixed shot.

clue.text: Peach smell Danish lady doctor bottles

parts.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell

indicators.note: the word for doctor holds the name within it

parts.note: Inge is a Danish woman's name

explanation.surface: A Danish woman doctor stores a peach that smells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peach' looks like the fruit; it means a splendid thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for something outstanding or excellent.

clue.text: Put s at the end of code to get codes

indicators.note: put means the letter is shifted to a new position
says where it goes: to the end of the code word

parts.note: Morse is the dot-and-dash code

explanation.surface: A grammar instruction for making a plural.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving S to the end of MORSE gives the Latin plural for customs.
explanation.definitionFit: Mores are the customs and conventions of a society, its codes of behaviour.

clue.text: Aboard tandem, I tow Teri around to take her for a ride

indicators.note: around means the carried letters are read backwards
the letters are aboard, carried within the words

explanation.surface: A cyclist pulls Teri on a tandem, taking her out.
explanation.walkthrough: EMITOWT sits inside 'tandem, I tow Teri'; 'around' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheat on a partner is to deceive them, take them for a ride.

clue.text: Soldiers back to back in service finally learning the ropes

indicators.note: the soldiers sit inside the service abbreviation

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, one of the armed services
two GIs, American soldiers, placed back to back read IG then GI

indicators.note: only the last letter of learning is wanted

explanation.surface: Soldiers in the service are finally learning the ropes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'learning the ropes' looks like one idiom; 'learning' gives G.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's ropes and cables supporting the masts and sails.

clue.text: Miserable bloody dog rejected hot tripe

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the words read backwards

parts.note: miserable means sad
blood is red
a lab is a Labrador dog

explanation.surface: A miserable dog refuses some hot tripe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' reverses SADREDLAB to BALDERDAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe in its figurative sense is worthless nonsense.

clue.text: Needing plenty of bread and honey

definitions.meaning: bread is slang for money, so it means expensive
honey is a term of endearment, like darling

explanation.surface: Bread and honey taking a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both costly and beloved.
